findings.title: question: the effects table has no trustline_created for a trustline a Stellar asset contract trust() call opens
findings.cause: transformEffects derives the effects of an InvokeHostFunction operation only from Stellar asset contract events (addInvokeHostFunctionEffects, internal/transform/effects.go L1326-L1440 at 2b24ec89), which turn transfer, mint, clawback and burn into credit and debit effects. A trustline the contract's trust() function opens (CAP-73) changes the ledger without such an event, so it gets no trustline_created effect, while a ChangeTrust operation that opens the same trustline does (addChangeTrustEffects, L647-L705). The source does not say whether this is intended.

findings.title: question: the effects table has no account_created for an account a Stellar asset contract transfer creates
findings.cause: An XLM transfer through the native asset contract to an account that does not exist creates it (CAP-73). transformEffects writes account_debited and account_credited for the transfer event (addInvokeHostFunctionEffects, internal/transform/effects.go L1326-L1440 at 2b24ec89) but account_created only for a CreateAccount operation (addAccountCreatedEffects, L411-L437), so the new account has no account_created effect. The source does not say whether this is intended.

findings.title: question: horizon.Offer reads an offer id given as "+16" or "-0"
findings.cause: horizon.Offer.ID is an int64 tagged `json:"id,string"`, so encoding/json unquotes the text and passes it to strconv.ParseInt, which takes an optional sign: "+16" reads as 16 and "-0" as 0, on every tested version (v0.7.1 to v0.9.0). The field reads horizon's own responses, which carry the canonical text, so the draft is a question. rs-stellar-xdr reads the same two strings the same way (RS-1, rs-stellar-xdr#627); the code is separate, so this is its own finding with RS-1 related.

findings.title: XDR decoders accept arrays, strings and opaque values longer than the schema allows
findings.cause: The generated decoders read a variable-length array, string or opaque with XdrDataInputStream.readArrayLength or readBytes, which bound the count only by the bytes left in the input (lib/src/xdr/xdr_data_io.dart L380-L394), and never check the maximum the schema declares: XdrSCSpecFunctionV0 reads `outputs<1>` with no bound (lib/src/xdr/xdr_sc_spec_function_v0.dart L63), XdrPreconditionsV2 reads `extraSigners<2>` the same way (lib/src/xdr/xdr_preconditions_v2.dart L102). 3.12.0 reads 101 operations, 21 signatures, a 29-byte text memo, a 33-byte symbol, a 65-byte data value, payload and signature, 6 path assets, 11 claimants, 3 extra signers and 2 spec outputs, all of which stellar-core refuses.

findings.title: XDR decoders read Soroban values and authorization trees nested deeper than stellar-core accepts
findings.cause: XdrDataInputStream counts only recursive type decodes, up to maxXdrDecodeDepth (500), and nested delegate signatures, up to maxRecursiveDecodeDepth (128) (lib/src/xdr/xdr_data_io.dart L316-L340). Neither is stellar-core's limit, which counts every nested type, so ScVal maps and vectors and SorobanAuthorizedInvocation trees past core's limit decode and the sdk reads envelopes core refuses; in the other direction, the candidate lane's ledgers with claim predicates, quorum sets or delegate signatures nested to core's ledger limit are refused. The same class as JS-DEPTH in js-stellar-sdk; separate code.

findings.title: XDR strings are decoded as UTF-8, so valid ledgers with other bytes in a memo, symbol or string do not decode
findings.cause: XdrDataInputStream.readString returns utf8.decode of the bytes (lib/src/xdr/xdr_data_io.dart L365-L367), which throws a FormatException on bytes that are not UTF-8. The XDR string type is bytes, and stellar-core applied transactions whose text memo, InvokeContractArgs function name, ScString or ScSymbol holds bytes that are not UTF-8; those fail to decode, which also stops decode_json, encode_json and the transaction hash. js-stellar-sdk#1823 is the same class: there the bytes are mangled instead of refused.

findings.title: ManageSellOfferOperationBuilder.setOfferId reads hex, signed, padded and out-of-range text as an offer id
findings.cause: toOperationBody passes the offer id text to BigInt.parse (lib/src/manage_sell_offer_operation.dart L111), which takes a sign, surrounding whitespace and a 0x prefix, and keeps any size, so "0x10", " 16 ", "+16" and "-0" read as 16 or 0, and 9223372036854775808 and 18446744073709551615 are written as the int64 -9223372036854775808 and -1. The text forms are the ones RS-1 (rs-stellar-xdr#627), GO-TEXTID and js-stellar-sdk#1907 accept; the wrap to another id is js-stellar-sdk#1785's. Separate code in each sdk.

findings.title: manage offer ids are an unsigned 64-bit type, so a negative offer id renders as a different XDR-JSON value and its XDR-JSON does not encode
findings.cause: XdrManageSellOfferOp.offerID is an XdrUint64 (lib/src/xdr/xdr_manage_sell_offer_op.dart L34), where the schema says int64. The bytes round trip, but XDR-JSON renders offer id -16 as "18446744073709551600" and refuses the canonical "-16" ("XdrUint64 holds -16, outside the range of a uint64").

findings.title: question: XDR-JSON rendering refuses a signed-payload signer with an empty payload
findings.cause: toXdrJsonValue renders a signed-payload signer as its P strkey, and StrKey refuses an empty payload (lib/src/key_pair.dart L433, "carries an empty payload, which has no strkey rendering"), so a transaction the network applied with such a signer has no XDR-JSON. SEP-51 gives the value no canonical form, so the question is whether refusing the whole document is the intended answer; stellar-xdr writes an <INVALID: marker instead.

findings.title: AbstractTransaction.fromEnvelopeXdr refuses an envelope with an inflation operation
findings.cause: Operation.fromXdr has no case for INFLATION and throws "Unknown operation body OperationType.9" (lib/src/operation.dart L258-L259), so the sdk cannot build a transaction object, nor its hash, for envelopes from before protocol 12 that core applied.

findings.title: XDR decoders accept values the schema forbids: arrays and strings past their maximum, nonzero padding, nesting past stellar-core's limit
findings.cause: XdrBuffer::readOpaqueVariable and readString take a maxLength the generated decoders never pass, and skip the padding without reading it (Soneso/StellarSDK/Xdr/XdrBuffer.php L158-L173); readArrayLength bounds a count only by the bytes left (XdrPreconditionsV2::decode reads extraSigners<2> with it, Xdr/XdrPreconditionsV2.php L74). Nesting is capped at DECODE_DEPTH_LIMIT (500) recursive decodes (Xdr/XdrBuffer.php L33), not core's limit. 1.18.0 reads 101 operations, 21 signatures, a 29-byte memo, a 33-byte symbol, 65-byte payloads, 6 path assets, 11 claimants, 3 extra signers, 2 spec outputs, nonzero padding in strings, bytes and signer keys, and ScVal and authorization trees past core's depth, all of which stellar-core refuses.

findings.title: 64-bit values above 2^63-1 and negative int64 values lose their XDR-JSON form
findings.cause: uint64 fields are php ints, which hold 2^64-1 as -1, and XdrJsonHelper::uint64ToString refuses negative ints (Soneso/StellarSDK/Xdr/XdrJsonHelper.php L290-L300), so a muxed id or memo id at or above 2^63 has no XDR-JSON. In the other direction XdrSequenceNumber is read as an unsigned BigInteger (Xdr/XdrBuffer.php readBigInteger64), so a bump_to of -1 renders as "18446744073709551615" where the schema's int64 says -1.

findings.title: inner transaction hashes and config upgrade content hashes render as the hex of their hex in XDR-JSON, and their XDR-JSON does not encode
findings.cause: XdrInnerTransactionResultPair and XdrConfigUpgradeSetKey keep their hash as hex text (bin2hex in decode, Soneso/StellarSDK/Xdr/XdrInnerTransactionResultPair.php L21 and Xdr/XdrConfigUpgradeSetKey.php L18), while the base classes' toJsonValue hex-encodes the field again (Xdr/XdrInnerTransactionResultPairBase.php L52), so XDR-JSON carries a 128-character string. Reading that JSON back fails ("Unexpected length for value. Has length 16, expected 32") or crashes with a TypeError in XdrEncoder::opaqueFixed. The bytes round trip; only XDR-JSON is wrong. Encoding the pair from a decoded value also raises php warnings (pack(): illegal hex digit) on stderr.

findings.cause: AbstractOperation::fromXdr has no case for INFLATION and throws "Unknown operation type: 9" (Soneso/StellarSDK/AbstractOperation.php L132), so the sdk cannot build a transaction object, nor its hash, for envelopes core applied before protocol 12. findings.title: MuxedAccount takes a negative id and writes it as the unsigned id it wraps to
findings.cause: MuxedAccount::__construct takes ?int $id and checks only the account (Soneso/StellarSDK/MuxedAccount.php L67-L74), so -1 and -16 become the muxed ids 18446744073709551615 and 18446744073709551600 when the account is encoded: a value that encodes a different id, the class of js-stellar-sdk#1785.

findings.title: asset ordering compares issuers as strkey text, so pool ids and change trust pool shares follow another order than the network

This is Beans-BV/dotnet-stellar-sdk#257, open; js-stellar-sdk#1766 fixed the same class.

findings.title: StrKey decoders accept claimable balance and signed payload strkeys SEP-23 refuses, and crash on a lone prefix letter
findings.cause: DecodeClaimableBalanceId checks only the version byte and checksum (StellarDotnetSdk/StrKey.cs L447-L450), so a balance id with sub-version 1 decodes; DecodeSignedPayload reads the payload with the XDR decoder and does not check that it consumed the whole strkey (L405-L420), so a payload one byte long or a length prefix shorter than the bytes decodes; DecodeVersionByte indexes the first decoded byte without a length check (L311-L314) and throws IndexOutOfRangeException for "M".

findings.title: Transaction.FromEnvelopeXdr refuses an ScVal vec whose body is absent
findings.cause: SCVal.FromXdr refuses SCV_VEC with an absent body ("SCV_VEC with an absent vector body", StellarDotnetSdk/Soroban/SCVal.cs L1753), which a contract's arguments can carry in an envelope core applied, so the transaction object and its hash cannot be built.

findings.title: the text memo decoder accepts 29 bytes
findings.cause: Memo.Decode reads the text with ReadString, which takes ReadVarOpaque(uint.MaxValue) (StellarDotnetSdk.Xdr/Memo.cs L72, XdrDataInputStream.cs L88-L91), not the string<28> bound, so a 29-byte memo that core refuses decodes.
